about: The level (constraint language 6.22, Y § 3.19) a call into each library needs, by module path: a call of a function under a path listed here, or of a method of a type under it, needs that level, and the longest path that matches wins. Every library a body calls into is listed, at least by its crate: a call into a library with no entry needs `effects`, since nothing says it has none. `bare-rust` takes the function a call resolves to from rustc where the woven crate builds (`crate::facts`), and else resolves it through the file's `use` declarations, and a method through its receiver's type when the constraint data gives it. A method of a trait needs the level of its type's module and of its trait's. A macro is listed by its path (`std::println`), and an invocation of it needs that level; a macro named alone is the prelude's (`std::…`) unless the file imports it. A macro whose source is at hand (a dependency's `#[macro_export]` macro, or the standard library's with the toolchain's `rust-src`) is read from its body instead, its calls at this table's levels, unless `macros_from_table` names it, with why. A procedural macro's expansion is read from the calls rustc resolved at its invocation. `bare-rust levels --libraries <crate>...` checks the table against what a library crate's code calls; `trusted` names the functions of a library that call more than their module's level for the library's own sake: each with the calls it vouches for (a path, or a module or type the call is under) and why. Only those calls are not counted; anything else the function calls is, and an entry whose calls the function no longer makes is reported.

y_runtime::shared::wait.why: waits for a commit on the deadline its caller gave it: the caller pays for the deadline (`y_runtime::Deadline::after`, at `effects`) and for the wait (`// y: waits until …`, at `effects`)

macros_from_table.std::thread_local: declares thread-local state, which is `shared`; its body expands into `std::thread::local_impl`, the standard library's own machinery
